evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 10.38 mg/L (t=50.0h) to 1.80 mg/L (t=50.2h) and continues to ~1.24-1.27 mg/L by t=51.8-52.0h, breaching the 2.0 mg/L minimum
All three source batches never fall below ~7.4 mg/L (e.g., source-1 min ~7.44 at 74.8h; source-2 ~8.18; source-3 ~8.09), so the receiving collapse is abnormal
Receiving P assay: 3.04 g/L at t=48h (available 52h) — production ongoing, so stop (zero counted production) is worst outcome
Forward model at t=52h: estimated transfer multiplier 0.40 (aeration fault); all bounded actions predicted infeasible

Model comparison: strong_feed_reduction post-decision deficit 7.95 mg·h/L, min DO 0.87 mg/L, product mass 193.99 kg; keep: 8.40/0.80/193.91; combined: 10.56/0.77/193.90; increase_air: 12.32/0.71/193.90; reduce_feed: 12.69/0.67/193.91
args.rationale: At t=52h the receiving fermenter has a severe, continuing DO2 collapse (10.4 → ~1.3 mg/L since t=50.2h), well below the 2.0 mg/L oxygen limit and far deeper than any source batch dip (~7.4-8 mg/L minimum). The forward model attributes this to a transfer-capacity fault (multiplier ≈0.40) rather than a transient OUR spike, so air increase alone (×1.15) cannot close the gap. The strongest available oxygen-demand reduction (feed to 0.6×) is the best bounded intervention: it cuts OUR ~40%, yields the lowest modeled post-decision oxygen deficit (7.95 mg·h/L) and highest modeled minimum DO (0.87 mg/L) among all actions including keep, while retaining essentially full product mass (~194 kg, terminal ~2.5 g/L). Stop is rejected because it yields zero counted production. No extra assay was requested: the critical variable (DO2) is already continuously observed, and the 4h-lag product assay cannot inform an urgent oxygen decision. Note the model itself flags no action as fully feasible, so this is a best-effort damage-limiting intervention; the underlying aeration fault should be escalated to engineering for repair regardless.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and may not match the hidden receiving realization; its transfer-fault estimate (0.40) and per-action DO predictions carry substantial uncertainty (sensitivity members span min DO 0.45-1.29 mg/L, product mass 172-212 kg, zero feasible members). If the collapse is actually a transient sensor artifact or a brief OUR excursion that self-recovers (as source dips did), a milder action (keep/increase_air) could have sufficed and the strong feed cut would cost some growth; conversely, if the aeration fault is worse than modeled, even this action leaves DO below the limit. The delayed product assay (P at 48h) lags by 4h, so current product state is uncertain.
